reasons: Deviation classification is correct: Section 5.1 provides only a care-and-skill warranty plus an authority rep, with no conformance warranty for Materials, no warranty period and no stated remedy, while 5.2 makes 5.1 exclusive and 5.4(c) puts all Materials 'AS IS' — this fails the fallback (90 days / 30 days with repair, re-performance or refund) and approaches walk-away for deliverables.

Redline is actionable and tracks the rule's redline guidance and model language: it inserts a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty, adds the repair/re-performance/refund remedy, and carves the express warranties out of the 'AS IS' disclaimer ('EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1'), leaving the existing professional/workmanlike language intact.

The failed deterministic check on warranty period is a false negative — the inserted text expressly states 'a period of ninety (90) days following delivery', which meets the fallback threshold; the 0.474 changed-character ratio on p0074 reflects the necessary carve-out prefix on an all-caps disclaimer, not an over-broad rewrite.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, and correctly explains both the gap and the carve-out; only minor placement nits (new subsection (c) after (b) which does not carry an 'and', and the remedy sentence following the compliance covenant paragraph) which do not affect substance.
